name: Give
label: Revelation
lede: Crucial John Scharbach named Give while deployed in Iraq, then spent six years pressing flower-covered 7"s for half the labels in hardcore before Revelation, the label that shaped his ear, put out the 12".

eras.title: Named in Iraq, born in Baltimore
eras.text: Scharbach had the name before he had a band, picked while stationed in Iraq. Give existed loosely from 2005 and got a lineup late in 2008, with a first show opening for Rival Schools.

years.h: Scharbach hears Gone, wants a G-word, and picks Give
years.p: Deployed in Iraq, he kept playing Gone and liked how the band's name read on its covers. He went looking for another short word starting with G.
years.xp:
In the DxR interview, Scharbach says: "I was listening to that band GONE a lot while I was over there." The name was settled before the band had members, and Give ran loosely from 2005.

His own influences, in his words: "Youth of Today, Nirvana, Ignition," plus "obscure 3rd and 4th tier stuff from the late 80's."

years.big: "It really got us motivated to practice almost everyday"
years.h: Give open for Rival Schools at Baltimore's Ottobar
years.p: Scharbach on the first show, November 2008. The second came soon after, with Mindset at a record release in Pennsylvania.
years.xp: Revelation dates the band's start to late 2008, which matches the Ottobar bill. The lineup Revelation lists today: Scharbach on vocals, Ian Marshall and Ben Schultz on guitar, Doug Free on bass, Gene Melkisethian on drums.

eras.title: Flowerheads, 7" by 7"
eras.text: Give released six 7"s on labels from React to Triple B, flew to Central America with Lion of Judah, and called their fans flowerheads. Members also played in Rival Mob, No Tolerance and Mob Mentality, and the band ran its own label, Moonflower.

years.cap: Poster for Give's Singles Going Confetti: the band in a flower frame
years.h: Give's 7"s pile up, and a 12" goes on their own Moonflower
years.p: Heaven Is Waiting (React), Boots of Faith (Deranged), Flowerhead (Youngblood), Petal Pushing (Painkiller) and I Am Love (Triple B).
years.xp:
By October 2014 Vice counted six 7"s, two 12"s and a cassette. Revelation's own bio says the same.

Fans were flowerheads. Vice quoted the band's line on the subject: "are you a flowerhead or not? If not, stay out of our faces..and our lives."

yt: hate5six, Le Poisson Rouge, New York, June 7, 2014
years.h: Give go to Central America with Lion of Judah
years.p: Back in the US they play with [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]], Code Orange Kids, [[Night Birds|c7a4d766-6bc7-4766-b86e-35e8d8e3fa43]] and Tenement.
years.xp: Scharbach says the Central America trip meant "a lot of good people" met. The interview, dated August 9, 2014, doesn't give dates for the tour.

years.h: The Electric Flower Circus is Give's first full-length
years.p: Thirteen songs on the band's own Moonflower Records, out October 28, 2014.
years.xp: Tony Rettman premiered it at Vice the day before, calling Give "one of the best bands working in the American Underground today."

years.h: Give spend November 2014 touring Europe, 26 stops in all
years.p: It starts in Cologne and ends in Wunstorf, Germany, with stops in Glasgow, Oslo, Budapest and Trento.
years.xp: Vice's list also covers Amsterdam, London, Copenhagen, Berlin, Vienna and Munich, among others.

eras.title: Clay flowers on Revelation
eras.text: Revelation's early catalog was where Scharbach's idea of music came from, so a Revelation 12" meant something. Don Zientara recorded it and clay art from Japan wrapped it.

years.cap: Give's guitarist, daisy shirt, mid-jump, taken by 2014
q: Revelation's early catalog changed the way I thought about music.
years.src: Discogs · Revelation Records: pressing · Punknews · DxR
years.h: Revelation presses Sonic Bloom on gold, red and tour-only black
years.p: Recorded by Zientara with clay art by Kinya Masuo. The 330 black copies were sold only on Give's January 2015 West Coast tour.
years.xp:
The songs are Sonic Bloom, Learning to Die, Brand New Flag and Eat the Rainbow. Revelation pressed 1,087 on gold (clear yellow, per Discogs) and 328 on red alongside the tour-only black.

Punknews called Give post-flowerchild punks, too trippy for easy comparisons.
